intro: Hi! You already know get up, turn off and look for. In this lesson you'll learn seventeen new phrasal verbs for work, people and problems, like put off, look after and run out of, and you'll learn where it, him and her go: put it off, but look after her. Warm-up: is there something you always put off?
teachingNotes: Build on a2-phrasal-verbs-common: the learner knows what a phrasal verb is (verb + small word with a new meaning), get up, wake up, turn on/off, put on, take off, look for, pick up, and the rule turn it on (not 'turn on it'). Recap it in a line; don't re-teach those. New B1 set in three groups. Work and plans: set up (mengatur, menyiapkan a meeting / a laptop; mendirikan a business), carry on (melanjutkan; + -ing or + with), put off (menunda, mengundur; + -ing too), call off (membatalkan), look into (memeriksa, menyelidiki a problem / complaint), fill in (mengisi a form; American fill out), hand in (menyerahkan, mengumpulkan). People: get on with (akur dengan; American get along with), look after (merawat, menjaga), look forward to (menantikan; + noun or -ing), run into (bertemu tanpa sengaja), turn down (menolak an offer / job / invitation). Problems: break down (mogok, rusak; no object), run out of (kehabisan), give up (berhenti a habit; menyerah; + -ing), sort out (membereskan; very British), find out (mencari tahu, jadi tahu; often + what / when / if).

Common errors: *'Please turn off it' → turn it off (and the same with the new ones: *'put off it', *'fill in it', *'handed in it'); *'I'm looking my keys' → looking for (mencari has no extra word); *'I gave up to smoke' → gave up smoking (Indonesian berhenti / untuk); *'I'm looking forward to see you' → to seeing (this to is part of the phrase, like to in go to the office, so a noun or -ing follows); *'fill the form' → fill in the form; *'we ran out petrol' → ran out of; *'she gived up' → gave up (the past goes on the verb, never on the small word).

put off vs call off is the key meaning trap (Indonesian diundur / ditunda vs batal; many say 'di-cancel'). put off = it still happens, later (until Friday, to next week); call off = it doesn't happen (money back, nobody goes). call off has nothing to do with phoning. Also: run into = meet by chance, meet = planned (both 'ketemu'); look for (mencari a thing) vs find out (mencari tahu information) vs look into (memeriksa a problem) vs look after (merawat).

Where the pronoun goes: present two lists to remember, without the words separable / inseparable. it / them / him / her in the middle: set it up, put it off, call it off, fill it in, hand it in, turn it down, sort it out, give it up (a noun may go in the middle or after: put the meeting off = put off the meeting). Never split, the word goes at the end: look after her, look into it, get on with him, look forward to it, run into him, run out of it. Tricks: three-word ones never split, and the look ones (look for / after / into) never split. break down and carry on have no object right after them (carry on with it). find out is usually + a question word or about (find out what happened, find out about it): don't drill 'find it out'.

Meaning from context: teach the learner to use clues (a new date → put off; money back → call off; car / lift + stopped → break down; no more petrol / money → run out of). turn down has two meanings: turn down a job / offer = menolak, turn down the music / the AC = mengecilkan. British vs American: fill in / fill out, get on with / get along with, petrol / gas, lift / elevator; sort out is more British.

Limits: grammar from A0–A2 only (present simple / continuous, past simple, present perfect with just / already / yet, going to, will, can / could, should / have to / must, first conditional, verb + to / -ing). No passive: say 'they called off the match', not 'the match was called off'. No past perfect, reported speech or second conditional. Don't add other phrasal verbs (come up with, put up with, get over, take after, bring up) unless the learner asks, and keep three-word verbs to the three in the lesson.

keyPoints.title: Phrasal verbs for work, people and problems
keyPoints.explanation: Learn each phrasal verb as a whole, like a new word, in three groups. Work and plans: set up (mengatur, menyiapkan), carry on (melanjutkan), put off (menunda, it happens later), call off (membatalkan, it doesn't happen), look into (memeriksa a problem), fill in (mengisi a form; American fill out), hand in (menyerahkan). People: get on with (akur dengan), look after (merawat, menjaga), look forward to (menantikan), run into (bertemu tanpa sengaja), turn down (menolak an offer). Problems: break down (mogok, rusak), run out of (kehabisan), give up (berhenti a habit, menyerah), sort out (membereskan), find out (mencari tahu). The context helps: a new date → put off; money back → call off.

examples.en: The manager is ill, so we're putting off the training until next week.
examples.id: Manajernya sakit, jadi pelatihannya kami undur sampai minggu depan.

examples.en: The airline called off our flight and gave us our money back.
examples.id: Maskapainya membatalkan penerbangan kami dan mengembalikan uang kami.

examples.en: I ran into my old classmate at Gambir station.
examples.id: Saya kebetulan ketemu teman sekelas lama saya di Stasiun Gambir.

id.title: Phrasal verb untuk kerja, orang dan masalah
id.explanation: Hafalkan setiap phrasal verb secara utuh, seperti kosakata baru, dalam tiga kelompok. Kerja dan rencana: set up (mengatur, menyiapkan), carry on (melanjutkan), put off (menunda, terjadinya nanti), call off (membatalkan, tidak jadi terjadi), look into (memeriksa masalah), fill in (mengisi formulir; bahasa Inggris Amerika: fill out), hand in (menyerahkan). Orang: get on with (akur dengan), look after (merawat, menjaga), look forward to (menantikan), run into (bertemu tanpa sengaja), turn down (menolak tawaran). Masalah: break down (mogok, rusak), run out of (kehabisan), give up (berhenti dari kebiasaan, menyerah), sort out (membereskan), find out (mencari tahu). Konteks membantu: ada tanggal baru → put off; uang dikembalikan → call off.

keyPoints.title: Using them in sentences
keyPoints.explanation: Phrasal verbs work like other verbs: the -s, -ing or past form goes on the verb, never on the small word: she looks after, we're putting off, it broke down, we ran out of, he gave up. After give up, look forward to, put off and carry on, a verb takes -ing: gave up smoking (not 'gave up to smoke'), looking forward to meeting you (not 'to meet'). Don't drop the small words: fill in a form (not 'fill the form'), run out of petrol (not 'run out petrol').

examples.en: My uncle gave up smoking last year.
examples.id: Paman saya berhenti merokok tahun lalu.

examples.en: We're looking forward to the holiday in Lombok.
examples.id: Kami tidak sabar menunggu liburan ke Lombok.

examples.en: Can you fill in this form, please?

id.title: Memakainya dalam kalimat
id.explanation: Phrasal verb bekerja seperti kata kerja lain: -s, -ing atau bentuk lampaunya ditaruh di kata kerjanya, tidak pernah di kata kecilnya: she looks after, we're putting off, it broke down, we ran out of, he gave up. Setelah give up, look forward to, put off dan carry on, kata kerja berikutnya pakai -ing: gave up smoking (bukan 'gave up to smoke'), looking forward to meeting you (bukan 'to meet'). Jangan buang kata kecilnya: fill in a form (bukan 'fill the form'), run out of petrol (bukan 'run out petrol').

keyPoints.title: it, him, her: in the middle or at the end?
keyPoints.explanation: Some phrasal verbs work like turn it off: a noun can go after the small word or in the middle, but it / them / him / her must go in the middle: set it up, put it off, call it off, fill it in, hand it in, turn it down, sort it out, give it up. Others never split: the word always goes at the end: look after her, look into it, get on with him, look forward to it, run into him, run out of it. There's no rule you can see, so learn the two lists. Tricks: the three-word ones and the look ones never split.

examples.en: The meeting? Let's put it off until Monday.
examples.id: Rapatnya? Kita undur saja sampai Senin.

examples.en: The kids? Don't worry, I'm looking after them.
examples.id: Anak-anak? Tenang, saya yang menjaga mereka.

examples.en: Sugar? Sorry, we've run out of it.

id.title: it, him, her: di tengah atau di akhir?
id.explanation: Sebagian phrasal verb bekerja seperti turn it off: kata benda boleh di belakang kata kecil atau di tengah, tapi it / them / him / her harus di tengah: set it up, put it off, call it off, fill it in, hand it in, turn it down, sort it out, give it up. Yang lain tidak pernah dipisah: katanya selalu di akhir: look after her, look into it, get on with him, look forward to it, run into him, run out of it. Tidak ada aturan yang kelihatan, jadi hafalkan dua daftar ini. Triknya: yang terdiri dari tiga kata dan yang diawali look tidak pernah dipisah.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read: 'The manager can't come today, so we're putting off the meeting until Thursday.' Is there going to be a meeting? Write yes or no.
guidedPractice.hint: put off = menunda: the meeting moves to Thursday, but it still happens.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with into, for or after: Your laptop is very slow? Don't worry, the IT team will look ___ it this afternoon.
guidedPractice.hint: The IT team is going to check the problem: look into = memeriksa.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of the verb in brackets: Sari is looking forward to ___ (start) her new job in Bandung.
guidedPractice.hint: After look forward to, a verb takes -ing.

guidedPractice.prompt: Put the words call, off and it in the right order: It's going to rain all day. Let's ___.
guidedPractice.hint: With it, the small word goes after it, like turn it off.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Dimas is very friendly. Everyone gets on him with.
expected: dimas is very friendly everyone gets on with him
dimas is very friendly everyone gets on well with him
everyone gets on well with him
guidedPractice.hint: get on with never splits: the person goes at the end.

independentPractice.prompt: Write one sentence about a habit you gave up, or want to give up. Use give up + -ing.
independentPractice.hint: For example: I gave up drinking ... / I want to give up eating ...

independentPractice.prompt: Write two sentences about your work or study with two phrasal verbs from this lesson, for example set up, put off, hand in or look into.
independentPractice.hint: For example: I have to hand in my report on Friday. My boss set up a meeting for Monday.

independentPractice.prompt: Read: 'Pak Hasan's car broke down on the toll road, so he took an ojek online to the office.' Why did Pak Hasan take an ojek? Answer in a few words.
independentPractice.hint: break down = mogok: the car stopped working.

assessment.prompt: Read the notice: 'Because of the heavy rain, the organisers have called off tonight's concert. You can get your money back at the ticket office.' Is the concert going to happen on another day? Write yes or no.
assessment.rubric: Correct: no. call off = membatalkan: the concert is not happening, and people get their money back. 'yes' = 0 (that would be put off = menunda, it happens later).

assessment.prompt: Read Dimas's message: 'Guess what! I ran into my old teacher at Blok M yesterday.' Did Dimas plan to meet his teacher? Write yes or no.
assessment.rubric: Correct: no. run into = bertemu tanpa sengaja: it was a surprise, not a plan. 'yes' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with a phrasal verb in the past simple (it means kehabisan): We ___ milk, so I went to the minimarket to buy some.
assessment.rubric: Correct: ran out of ('had run out of' is also correct). 'run out of' = 50 (the past is needed: ran). 'ran out' without of = 40 (run out of + thing needs of). 'runned out of' = 40. 'finished' = 0 (the task asks for a phrasal verb).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Budi gave up to drink sweet tea because of his health.
acceptableAnswers: budi gave up drinking sweet tea because of his health
budi gave up sweet tea because of his health
assessment.rubric: Correct: Budi gave up drinking sweet tea because of his health ('gave up sweet tea' is also correct). 'gave up drink' = 30 (after give up, the verb takes -ing). 'gives up drinking' = 60 (the past is needed). 'Budi stopped drinking sweet tea' = 60 (correct English, but the task is to fix give up). The sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Thanks for the invitation! I'm really looking forward to see you on Saturday.
acceptableAnswers: thanks for the invitation i'm really looking forward to seeing you on saturday
thanks for the invitation i am really looking forward to seeing you on saturday
thanks for the invitation im really looking forward to seeing you on saturday
i'm really looking forward to seeing you on saturday
i am really looking forward to seeing you on saturday
im really looking forward to seeing you on saturday
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm really looking forward to seeing you on Saturday. The to in look forward to is part of the phrase, so -ing follows. 'looking forward to saw you' = 0. 'looking forward see you' = 20 (to is missing and no -ing). 'I really look forward to seeing you' = 90 (correct, a little more formal). The sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Sari finished the report last night and handed in it this morning.
acceptableAnswers: sari finished the report last night and handed it in this morning
assessment.rubric: Correct: Sari finished the report last night and handed it in this morning. With it, the small word goes after it: handed it in. 'handed in the report' = 70 (correct, but repeats the report instead of using it). 'hand it in' = 60 (the past is needed: handed). The sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Put the words after, us and look in the right order (change the verb form if needed): When our parents are at work, our grandmother ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: looks after us. look after never splits, so us goes at the end, and our grandmother = she, so the verb takes -s: looks. 'look after us' = 70 (the -s is missing). 'looks us after' = 0 (this is the mistake being tested). 'looks after we' = 40 (after a verb or small word, use us, not we).

material.title: Work and plans: set up, put off, call off …

blocks.text:
**Quick recap** from A2: a **phrasal verb** is a **verb** (an action word) + a **small word** (*up, on, off, in, into, for* …) with a **new meaning**: *get up, turn off, look for, pick up*. With **it / them** the small word goes after: *turn **it** off*. Now seven new ones for **work and plans**:
- **set up** = mengatur, menyiapkan (a meeting, a new laptop); mendirikan (a business)
- **carry on** = lanjut, melanjutkan (*carry on + -ing*, or *carry on with + thing*)
- **put off** = menunda, mengundur ke waktu lain (*put off + -ing* too)
- **call off** = membatalkan (it won't happen at all)
- **look into** = memeriksa, menyelidiki (a problem, a complaint)
- **fill in** = mengisi (a form); American English says **fill out**
- **hand in** = menyerahkan, mengumpulkan (a report, homework, a form)

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat** dari A2: **phrasal verb** adalah **kata kerja** (kata untuk kegiatan) + **kata kecil** (*up, on, off, in, into, for* …) dengan **arti baru**: *get up, turn off, look for, pick up*. Dengan **it / them**, kata kecilnya ditaruh di belakang: *turn **it** off*. Sekarang tujuh yang baru untuk **kerja dan rencana**:
- **set up** = mengatur, menyiapkan (rapat, laptop baru); mendirikan (usaha)
- **carry on** = lanjut, melanjutkan (*carry on + -ing*, atau *carry on with + benda*)
- **put off** = menunda, mengundur ke waktu lain (bisa juga *put off + -ing*)
- **call off** = membatalkan (tidak jadi sama sekali)
- **look into** = memeriksa, menyelidiki (masalah, keluhan)
- **fill in** = mengisi (formulir); bahasa Inggris Amerika bilang **fill out**
- **hand in** = menyerahkan, mengumpulkan (laporan, PR, formulir)

rows.en: Can you set up a meeting with the client for Monday?
rows.id: Bisa atur rapat dengan klien untuk hari Senin?

rows.en: We had a short break and then carried on working.
rows.id: Kami istirahat sebentar lalu lanjut bekerja.

rows.en: I always put off going to the dentist.
rows.id: Saya selalu menunda pergi ke dokter gigi.

rows.en: It was raining hard, so they called off the football match.
rows.id: Hujannya deras, jadi pertandingan sepak bolanya dibatalkan.
rows.note: call off: the match didn't happen

rows.en: The IT team is looking into the problem with the Wi-Fi.
rows.id: Tim IT sedang memeriksa masalah Wi-Fi-nya.

rows.en: Please fill in this form and hand it in at reception.
rows.id: Tolong isi formulir ini lalu serahkan ke resepsionis.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: **diundur / ditunda** and **batal** are different, but many people just say *di-cancel*. **put off** = it's going to happen **later**: *put the meeting off **until Friday***. **call off** = it's **not going to happen**: *they called off the concert, everyone got their money back*. Look for clues: a new day or time (*until, to next week*) → put off; money back, nobody goes → call off. And *call off* has nothing to do with phoning someone.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **diundur / ditunda** dan **batal** itu berbeda, tapi banyak orang cuma bilang *di-cancel*. **put off** = tetap terjadi, tapi **nanti**: *put the meeting off **until Friday*** (rapatnya diundur sampai Jumat). **call off** = **tidak jadi** terjadi: *they called off the concert, everyone got their money back* (konsernya batal, semua orang dapat uangnya kembali). Cari petunjuknya: ada hari atau jam baru (*until, to next week*) → put off; uang kembali, tidak ada yang datang → call off. Dan *call off* tidak ada hubungannya dengan menelepon orang.

blocks.text: *Mengisi formulir* → **fill in** a form, not 'fill the form'. The small word is needed, like *for* in *look for*. British English uses **fill in** more, American English **fill out**: both are correct.

id.text: *Mengisi formulir* → **fill in** a form, bukan 'fill the form'. Kata kecilnya wajib ada, seperti *for* di *look for*. Bahasa Inggris British lebih sering pakai **fill in**, bahasa Inggris Amerika **fill out**: keduanya benar.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'The airline called off our flight, and they gave us our money back.' What happened to the flight?
blocks.explain: call off = membatalkan: the flight didn't happen, and that's why they gave the money back. If it only left later, that's a delay, not call off.

id.prompt: Baca: 'The airline called off our flight, and they gave us our money back.' Apa yang terjadi dengan penerbangannya?
id.explain: call off = membatalkan: penerbangannya tidak jadi, makanya uangnya dikembalikan. Kalau hanya berangkat lebih lambat, itu namanya terlambat, bukan call off.

id.title: Kerja dan rencana: set up, put off, call off …

material.title: People: get on with, look after, run into …

blocks.text:
Five phrasal verbs about **people**:
- **get on with** someone = akur, cocok dengan. Often with *well*: *I get on **well** with my neighbours.* American English says **get along with**.
- **look after** = merawat, menjaga (children, a sick person, a pet, a house)
- **look forward to** = menantikan, tidak sabar menunggu (something good in the future)
- **run into** someone = bertemu tanpa sengaja, kebetulan ketemu
- **turn down** = menolak (an offer, a job, an invitation)

id.text:
Lima phrasal verb tentang **orang**:
- **get on with** seseorang = akur, cocok dengan. Sering dengan *well*: *I get on **well** with my neighbours.* Bahasa Inggris Amerika bilang **get along with**.
- **look after** = merawat, menjaga (anak, orang sakit, hewan peliharaan, rumah)
- **look forward to** = menantikan, tidak sabar menunggu (sesuatu yang menyenangkan di masa depan)
- **run into** seseorang = bertemu tanpa sengaja, kebetulan ketemu
- **turn down** = menolak (tawaran, pekerjaan, undangan)

rows.en: Rina gets on well with her colleagues.
rows.id: Rina akur dengan rekan-rekan kerjanya.

rows.en: Sari looks after her grandmother on weekends.
rows.id: Sari merawat neneknya setiap akhir pekan.

rows.en: We're looking forward to the holiday in Lombok.
rows.id: Kami tidak sabar menunggu liburan ke Lombok.

rows.en: I'm looking forward to meeting your family.
rows.id: Saya tidak sabar bertemu keluargamu.

rows.en: I ran into Pak Hasan at the mall yesterday.
rows.id: Kemarin saya kebetulan ketemu Pak Hasan di mal.

rows.en: Dimas turned down the invitation because he was too tired.
rows.id: Dimas menolak undangan itu karena dia terlalu capek.

blocks.text: **look forward to + -ing**: this *to* is **not** the *to* of *want to go*. It's part of the phrase, like *to* in *go to the office*, so after it comes a **thing** or a verb with **-ing**: I'm looking forward **to the weekend** / **to meeting** you. Never 'looking forward to meet you'. Indonesian *tidak sabar **untuk** bertemu* makes this mistake very common.

id.text: **look forward to + -ing**: *to* di sini **bukan** *to* seperti di *want to go*. Ini bagian dari frasanya, seperti *to* di *go to the office*, jadi setelahnya datang **benda** atau kata kerja dengan **-ing**: I'm looking forward **to the weekend** / **to meeting** you. Jangan pernah 'looking forward to meet you'. Karena bahasa Indonesia bilang *tidak sabar **untuk** bertemu*, kesalahan ini sangat sering terjadi.

blocks.text: *Ketemu* has two English words. **meet** = you planned it: *I'm meeting Rina at six.* **run into** = a surprise, you didn't plan it: *I ran into Rina at the KRL station.* So 'I ran into my boss at the meeting' sounds strange: a meeting is planned.

id.text: *Ketemu* punya dua kata dalam bahasa Inggris. **meet** = sudah direncanakan: *I'm meeting Rina at six.* **run into** = kejutan, tidak direncanakan: *I ran into Rina at the KRL station.* Jadi 'I ran into my boss at the meeting' terdengar aneh: rapat itu direncanakan.

blocks.prompt: My parents are getting old, so I ___ them on weekends.
blocks.explain: look after = merawat, menjaga: you take care of your parents. look for = mencari (they're not lost), and look into = memeriksa a problem.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: My parents are getting old, so I ___ them on weekends.
id.explain: look after = merawat, menjaga: kamu merawat orang tuamu. look for = mencari (mereka tidak hilang), dan look into = memeriksa masalah.

id.title: Orang: get on with, look after, run into …

material.title: Problems: break down, run out of, give up …

blocks.text:
Five phrasal verbs for **problems** and how to deal with them:
- **break down** = mogok, rusak (a car, a motorbike, the lift, a machine). Nothing comes right after it: *My car broke down.*
- **run out of** = kehabisan (petrol, money, time, rice). Three words: don't forget **of**.
- **give up** = berhenti (a habit) or menyerah. With a verb: **give up + -ing**.
- **sort out** = membereskan, menyelesaikan (a problem, a mess). Very common in British English.
- **find out** = mencari tahu, jadi tahu (information: a time, a price, the truth). Often + *what / when / where / if*: *find out **what** happened*.
In the past, change only the **verb**, never the small word: break → **broke** down, run → **ran** out of, give → **gave** up, find → **found** out.

id.text:
Lima phrasal verb untuk **masalah** dan cara mengatasinya:
- **break down** = mogok, rusak (mobil, motor, lift, mesin). Tidak ada benda langsung setelahnya: *My car broke down.*
- **run out of** = kehabisan (bensin, uang, waktu, beras). Tiga kata: jangan lupa **of**.
- **give up** = berhenti (dari kebiasaan) atau menyerah. Dengan kata kerja: **give up + -ing**.
- **sort out** = membereskan, menyelesaikan (masalah, kekacauan). Sangat umum di bahasa Inggris British.
- **find out** = mencari tahu, jadi tahu (informasi: jam, harga, kebenaran). Sering + *what / when / where / if*: *find out **what** happened*.
Dalam bentuk lampau, ubah **kata kerjanya** saja, kata kecilnya tidak pernah berubah: break → **broke** down, run → **ran** out of, give → **gave** up, find → **found** out.

rows.en: My motorbike broke down on the way to the office.
rows.id: Motor saya mogok di jalan ke kantor.

rows.en: We've run out of rice. Can you buy some?
rows.id: Beras kita habis. Bisa tolong belikan?

rows.en: I ran out of petrol on the toll road.
rows.id: Saya kehabisan bensin di jalan tol.

rows.en: My uncle gave up smoking last year.
rows.id: Paman saya berhenti merokok tahun lalu.

rows.en: Don't worry, I'll sort it out.
rows.id: Tenang, nanti saya bereskan.

rows.en: Can you find out what time the train leaves?
rows.id: Bisa cari tahu jam berapa keretanya berangkat?

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: *berhenti merokok* → **give up smoking** (or *stop smoking*), never 'give up to smoke'. After **give up**, the verb takes **-ing**, the same as after *enjoy* or *finish*. Without a thing after it, *give up* = menyerah: *Don't give up!*

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *berhenti merokok* → **give up smoking** (atau *stop smoking*), jangan pernah 'give up to smoke'. Setelah **give up**, kata kerjanya pakai **-ing**, sama seperti setelah *enjoy* atau *finish*. Kalau tidak ada benda setelahnya, *give up* = menyerah: *Don't give up!*

blocks.text: Three verbs with *cari* in Indonesian: **look for** = mencari a thing or a person (*look for my keys*). **find out** = mencari tahu information (*find out the price*). **look into** = memeriksa a problem carefully, often at work (*We'll look into your complaint*).

id.text: Tiga kata kerja yang dalam bahasa Indonesia ada *cari*-nya: **look for** = mencari benda atau orang (*look for my keys*). **find out** = mencari tahu informasi (*find out the price*). **look into** = memeriksa masalah dengan teliti, sering di kantor (*We'll look into your complaint*).

material.title: put it off, but look after her

blocks.text:
You know this from A2: *turn the light off* = *turn off the light*, but with **it** only *turn **it** off*. Many new phrasal verbs work the same way: a noun can go after the small word **or** in the middle, but **it, them, me, him, her** (short words that replace a thing or a person) **must go in the middle**:
- set up → set **it** up
- put off → put **it** off
- call off → call **it** off
- fill in → fill **it** in
- hand in → hand **it** in
- turn down → turn **it** down
- sort out → sort **it** out
- give up → give **it** up
Others **never split**: the person or thing always goes **at the end**, even *him, her, it*:
- look after → look after **her**
- look into → look into **it**
- get on with → get on with **him**
- look forward to → look forward to **it**
- run into → run into **him**
- run out of → run out of **it**

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu ini dari A2: *turn the light off* = *turn off the light*, tapi dengan **it** hanya *turn **it** off*. Banyak phrasal verb baru bekerja dengan cara yang sama: kata benda boleh di belakang kata kecil **atau** di tengah, tapi **it, them, me, him, her** (kata pendek pengganti benda atau orang) **harus di tengah**:
- set up → set **it** up
- put off → put **it** off
- call off → call **it** off
- fill in → fill **it** in
- hand in → hand **it** in
- turn down → turn **it** down
- sort out → sort **it** out
- give up → give **it** up
Yang lain **tidak pernah dipisah**: orang atau bendanya selalu **di akhir**, termasuk *him, her, it*:
- look after → look after **her**
- look into → look into **it**
- get on with → get on with **him**
- look forward to → look forward to **it**
- run into → run into **him**
- run out of → run out of **it**

blocks.text: There's no rule you can see, so **learn the two lists**. Two tricks help: the **three-word** ones (*get on with, look forward to, run out of*) never split, and the **look** ones (*look for, look after, look into*) never split. *break down* and *carry on* have no thing right after them, so there's nothing to move (*carry on **with** it*).

id.text: Tidak ada aturan yang kelihatan, jadi **hafalkan dua daftar ini**. Ada dua trik: yang terdiri dari **tiga kata** (*get on with, look forward to, run out of*) tidak pernah dipisah, dan yang diawali **look** (*look for, look after, look into*) juga tidak pernah dipisah. *break down* dan *carry on* tidak langsung diikuti benda, jadi tidak ada yang perlu dipindah (*carry on **with** it*).

blocks.prompt: The client wants a new date for the meeting. Which sentence is correct?

blocks.explain: put off splits, and with it the small word goes after it: put it off. 'put off it' is the same mistake as 'turn off it', and off can't go at the end of the sentence.

id.title: put it off, tapi look after her

material.title: Guess the meaning from the context

blocks.text:
At B1 you'll meet phrasal verbs in emails, messages and the news. When you don't know one, use the **context** (the words and the situation around it):
- a new day or time → **put off**; money back, it's not happening → **call off**
- a problem, a complaint → **look into** / **sort out**
- a car, a lift, a machine + it stopped → **break down**
- no more petrol, money, time → **run out of**
- an offer, a job, an invitation + no → **turn down**
Some phrasal verbs have **two meanings**, and only the context tells you which. You saw **pick up** in A2. **turn down** is another one: *turn down **a job*** = menolak, but *turn down **the music / the AC*** = mengecilkan (make it quieter or lower).

id.text:
Di B1 kamu akan bertemu phrasal verb di email, pesan dan berita. Kalau ada yang tidak kamu tahu, pakai **konteksnya** (kata-kata dan situasi di sekitarnya):
- hari atau jam baru → **put off**; uang kembali, tidak jadi → **call off**
- masalah, keluhan → **look into** / **sort out**
- mobil, lift, mesin + berhenti → **break down**
- tidak ada lagi bensin, uang, waktu → **run out of**
- tawaran, pekerjaan, undangan + bilang tidak → **turn down**
Ada phrasal verb yang punya **dua arti**, dan hanya konteksnya yang memberi tahu arti yang mana. Kamu sudah melihat **pick up** di A2. **turn down** juga begitu: *turn down **a job*** = menolak, tapi *turn down **the music / the AC*** = mengecilkan (suaranya lebih pelan atau suhunya lebih rendah).

blocks.text: Read the **whole** sentence before you guess. *We've called off the trip* + *you'll get your money back* → the trip is not happening. *We've put off the trip* + *until March* → it's still happening, just later.

id.text: Baca **seluruh** kalimatnya sebelum menebak. *We've called off the trip* + *you'll get your money back* → perjalanannya batal. *We've put off the trip* + *until March* → perjalanannya tetap jadi, hanya diundur.

blocks.prompt: Read the email: 'Hi Rina, the printer on the third floor isn't working. Don't worry, the IT team is looking into it.' What is the IT team doing?
blocks.explain: look into = memeriksa, menyelidiki: the IT team is checking the problem. The clue is 'isn't working': there's a problem to look into.

id.prompt: Baca emailnya: 'Hi Rina, the printer on the third floor isn't working. Don't worry, the IT team is looking into it.' Apa yang sedang dilakukan tim IT?
id.explain: look into = memeriksa, menyelidiki: tim IT sedang memeriksa masalahnya. Petunjuknya 'isn't working': ada masalah yang perlu diperiksa.
